subject: Proposal: notice-handback & split-defense approach for Order Form indemnity
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@novarisk.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.example.com
Cc: procurement@novarisk.com
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form indemnity — initial redlines and evidence expectations

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked us to surface the legal team's redlines on indemnity and evidence handling for the Order Form / MSA. We've attached an annotated version of your standard MSA with inline comments (NovaRisk_redlines_MSA.docx). High-level concerns:

- Defense control: they want the right to defend claims alleging IP infringement for outputs that unequivocally arise from their integration, and to control settlement for business-impacting claims.
- Notice & timing: 30 days to provide detailed notice and supporting logs/evidence; they expect Redwood to accept notice by email to procurement@novarisk.com.
- Third-party OSS claims: they want a carveout for claims arising solely from NovaRisk's customer-supplied data and third-party OSS, unless Redwood introduced or trained on that OSS.
- Evidence sharing: tight SLA for evidence handback — they asked for a 10-business-day window to produce proof-of-origin artifacts from Redwood.

Can we confirm what we can accept for the Order Form? Procurement is trying to lock this into a pilot contract next week and wants a short mutual action plan if we can agree on the high-level approach.

Appreciate a quick reply.

Thanks,
Elaine Park\Head of Legal Operations\NovaRisk Health

Attachment: NovaRisk_redlines_MSA.docx (annotated redline)

From: ben_carter@redwood.example.com
To: Elaine Park <elaine@novarisk.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form indemnity — initial redlines and evidence expectations

Elaine — thanks for sending these over and for the clear summary. Looping in Kimberly and Marissa from our legal/contracts side so they can take the redlines and recommend language. 

High-level proposal from my side (for the pilot Order Form only):

1) Notice & handback: Accept a 30-day notice window. We propose a "notice-handback" flow: NovaRisk sends the notice to procurement@novarisk.com and redwood-legal@redwood.example.com; Redwood will triage and, where appropriate, offer to defend. If Redwood declines (because the claim stems solely from customer data/third-party OSS), we will provide an evidence pack and a short statement of technical facts within 10 business days to help NovaRisk defend.

2) Defense control split: Prefer default Redwood right to assume defense for third-party IP claims that implicate model outputs; we are open to a limited carveout for explicit customer modifications / customer-supplied models where NovaRisk accepts defense. We can add a narrow settlement consent clause (mutual consent for settlements that impose non-monetary obligations).

3) OSS carveout: Agree in principle to exclude pre-existing third-party OSS claims where NovaRisk can show the claim arises exclusively from OSS they configured or supplied. We will not accept broad OSS carveouts tied to training data unless there is clarity on provenance.

Kimberly/Marissa — can you review and (a) mark up NovaRisk's redline, and (b) suggest a concise operational paragraph I can send back to them that captures the notice-handback and evidence SLA? If we can pilot the approach on a single Order Form with a 6-month review, that may be the quickest path.

Ben
Enterprise Account Executive\Redwood Inference\(415) 555-0192

Attachment: ben_proposed_handback_paragraph.docx

From: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.example.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com, jonas_weber@redwood.example.com
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form indemnity — initial redlines and evidence expectations

Thanks Ben — reviewed NovaRisk's redlines and Ben's proposal. I attached a concise set of substitute paragraphs (kim_suggested_msa_paragraphs.pdf) that we should propose back. Summary of legal position and recommended edits: 

- Notice: we can accept the 30-day notice window. We will require (i) reasonably detailed allegation, (ii) scope of affected API calls, and (iii) any customer-provided artifacts. Redwood will acknowledge within 3 business days and provide an initial triage statement within 10 business days.

- Defense control: offer a default right-to-defend for Redwood for third-party IP claims tied to model output. Add narrow exceptions where the claim demonstrably arises solely from (a) customer-supplied models or (b) post-delivery customer modifications that materially alter output. Language: "Where Customer's use or configuration of the Service or Customer Data is the sole proximate cause of an IP claim, Customer may elect to assume defense; otherwise, Supplier (Redwood) may assume defense."

- Settlement approvals: include joint-consent language for settlements that impose ongoing obligations or material payment obligations beyond insurance coverage. Routine monetary settlements under an agreed threshold (we propose $50k) may be settled without prior consent if no injunctive relief or product changes are required.

- OSS/Third-party claims: propose an evidentiary trigger: Customer must produce provenance showing claim arises from third-party OSS. If provenance is not produced within 20 business days, Redwood retains right to assume defense.

Operational asks:
- We should offer a one-Order-Form pilot with a 6-month review, and require a narrow scope of evidence exchange to preserve customer confidentiality.
- Recommend adding an "evidence escrow" step that defines format and a secure transfer (SFTP or secure drive link) for logs and model trace.

I'll circulate the marked-up redline with tracked changes and a short explanation for procurement. If procurement pushes on OSS carveouts, we can offer a compromise: a structured provenance matrix and an explicit proof-of-origin milestone tied to the pilot.

Kimberly Park\Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts\Redwood Inference

Attachment: kim_suggested_msa_paragraphs.pdf

From: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
To: Elaine Park <elaine@novarisk.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.example.com, kimberly_park@redwood.example.com, jonas_weber@redwood.example.com
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form indemnity — initial redlines and evidence expectations

Elaine — thanks for the patience. Attaching our redline response and an operational playbook for the pilot Order Form. Short summary of what we can commit to for the pilot: 

1) Notice & evidence timeline: NovaRisk provides notice to procurement@novarisk.com and redwood-legal@redwood.example.com. Redwood acknowledges within 3 business days. Within 10 business days Redwood will either (a) offer to assume defense and provide defense counsel contacts, or (b) provide an evidence pack consisting of relevant model metadata, call traces, and a statement of technical facts.

2) Defense split and settlement: Redwood will assume defense for claims that are not demonstrably caused solely by customer-supplied models or customer modifications. For settlements that create ongoing obligations or product changes, we require prior written consent; for purely monetary settlements under $50,000 we can settle if agreed by counsel.

3) OSS / provenance: we will accept an OSS carveout where Customer supplies verifiable provenance within 20 business days. Absent provenance, Redwood will preserve defense rights.

4) Pilot governance: limited to the Order Form under deal NRH-2026-042 for 6 months. At 90 days we will run a joint checkpoint to review any notices/near-miss events and at 6 months either roll into standard terms or iterate language.

Next steps: 1) Elaine — confirm NovaRisk can operate under the pilot governance and the evidence escrow approach; 2) If yes, Ben will send the pilot Order Form draft and we will attach the tracked redline; 3) Procurement / Legal can sign DocuSign for the pilot Order Form (we can support a signature lane in HubSpot).

If NovaRisk needs an exec-level approval for the pilot scope (e.g., to accept the $50k routine settlement threshold), we can pull in our VP Legal for a single exception approval.

Thanks and speak soon,
Marissa Cole\Director, Contracts & Compliance\Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_response_redline.docx; Pilot_evidence_playbook.pdf
